note: Every environment variable the shipped Bash reads, sets for a child, or strips from one. Derived from bin/crossrev, lib/*.sh and lib/adapters/*.sh, and from lib/harnesses.json for the names an adapter resolves at run time. Bash's own variables (BASH_SOURCE, SECONDS, IFS, the positional parameters) are out, and so is every shell global initialised at source time, because an inherited value cannot survive the assignment. Each `shell` entry was read back with sed before it was written down. A variable whose `spelled` is false is never written out in the shell: the shell reaches it through an indirect expansion of a descriptor field, or — for PATH — through `command -v`.

dynamic.endpoint token: lib/adapters/claude.sh:82 reads `${!tok_env:-}`, where tok_env is the endpoint block's token_env key (lib/config.sh:375). The name is the operator's, so no table can hold it. templates/operator-config.yml:25 ships KIMI_API_KEY as the worked example.
dynamic.harness secret fallback: lib/auth.sh:990 falls back to CROSSREV_<HARNESS>_AUTH when the descriptor names no secret. Measured against lib/harnesses.json: the only harness with `refresher: true` is codex, and codex declares CROSSREV_CODEX_AUTH, so the fallback is unreachable in the shipped descriptor. CROSSREV_CLAUDE_AUTH and CROSSREV_AGY_AUTH are therefore not listed.

variables.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
variables.why: The billing signal: with it set and the harness keeping it, a run was charged to an API key rather than to a subscription. It survives the strip for claude alone, through the descriptor's env_keep.

variables.name: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
variables.why: Set on the claude invocation when an endpoint is configured, and refused when CrossRev inherited one: it redirects the harness process-wide, so a leak silently moves both legs onto one model.

variables.name: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
variables.why: The other half of the endpoint pair, refused for the same reason.

variables.name: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
variables.why: Claude's subscription credential. The shell never writes the name: it comes from .credential.secret and is read through `${!secret}`.

variables.name: CODEX_HOME
variables.why: Where codex keeps its credential. Read directly for the rollout file, and exported by the staging path as .credential.staging.env.

variables.name: CROSSREV_APP_SLUG
variables.why: The App whose comments count as CrossRev's own. Unset, an automated run trusts an author that does not exist and reads no markers.

variables.name: CROSSREV_ASSUME_YES
variables.why: `--yes` sets it, and only the value 1 answers every question. Nothing initialises it at source time, so an exported value reaches ui_confirm; measured with `CROSSREV_ASSUME_YES=1 ui_confirm ... </dev/null`, which answered yes where the bare call refused for want of a terminal.

variables.name: CROSSREV_CODEX_AUTH
variables.why: Codex's rotating credential, named by the descriptor and read through `${!secret}`. Stripped even from codex, because by then it has been written into CODEX_HOME.

variables.name: CROSSREV_DIFF_EXCLUDE
variables.why: One of three set on a single awk invocation and read back out of ENVIRON. Never exported.

variables.name: CROSSREV_DIFF_PATH
variables.why: As above.

variables.name: CROSSREV_DIFF_SIDE
variables.why: As above.

variables.name: CROSSREV_GIT_EMAIL
variables.why: The author a pushed fix is committed as, and the address a prior commit is recognised by. Defaults to crossrev@users.noreply.github.com.

variables.name: CROSSREV_GIT_NAME
variables.why: The name a pushed fix is committed under. Defaults to crossrev.

variables.name: CROSSREV_GROK_AUTH
variables.why: Grok's rotating credential, named by the descriptor.

variables.name: CROSSREV_HARNESS_FILE
variables.why: Points both descriptor readers at a file other than lib/harnesses.json. It is what every parity fixture on this branch uses to hand the shell a descriptor of its own.

variables.name: CROSSREV_HARNESS_INSTALL
variables.why: The install lines for a generated workflow, handed to one awk invocation through ENVIRON.

variables.name: CROSSREV_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS
variables.why: How many days a run directory survives the sweep, defaulting to 14. Nothing initialises it at source time; measured by intercepting find, which received -mtime +99 for an exported 99 and +14 for none.

variables.name: CROSSREV_NO_TIPS
variables.why: Suppresses the automated-mode suggestion. Only the value 1 suppresses it.

variables.name: CROSSREV_OPENCODE_AUTH
variables.why: Opencode's credential, named by the descriptor.

variables.name: CROSSREV_OWNER
variables.why: Which owner's App metadata the trusted-author slug is read from when CROSSREV_APP_SLUG is unset.

variables.name: CROSSREV_TRANSCRIPT_BASE
variables.why: The stem an attempt's captured streams are written under. The orchestrator sets it in its own process before calling an adapter (lib/run.sh:819); nothing initialises it at source time, so an exported value reaches the same read.

variables.name: GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN
variables.why: One of the four forge credentials stripped before a model-facing process. `gh help environment` lists it and GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN in order of precedence, so both are named.

variables.name: GH_TOKEN
variables.why: The ADR 0001 boundary: no GitHub credential reaches the process that reads attacker-controlled text.

variables.name: GITHUB_ACTIONS
variables.why: True on any runner, hosted or self-hosted. It decides only which unauthenticated-gh message is printed, and deliberately does not decide whether a secret is expected.

variables.name: GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN
variables.why: The second Enterprise name, and the credential in use whenever the first is unset.

variables.name: GITHUB_RUN_ID
variables.why: Names the run in the marker and in the run directory. Falls back to local-$$ off a runner.

variables.name: GITHUB_TOKEN
variables.why: As GH_TOKEN.

variables.name: GIT_INDEX_FILE
variables.why: Points one git invocation at a scratch index so the working tree's own index is untouched. Set per command, never exported.

variables.name: GROK_HOME
variables.why: Grok's staging lever, exported at a scratch directory for the leg and restored afterwards. The name is the descriptor's.

variables.name: HOME
variables.why: The fallback under every XDG path, and the directory a rotated key is collected from.

variables.name: LC_ALL
variables.why: Pinned to C on each text tool so awk, grep, sed and tr count bytes and fold ASCII only. Set per command.

variables.name: NO_COLOR
variables.why: Any value at all turns the palette off (https://no-color.org).

variables.name: OPENCODE_CONFIG
variables.why: The isolation config for one opencode invocation, merged over the operator's own and winning on the permission keys.

variables.name: OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR
variables.why: An empty directory, which displaces the agents and commands that would otherwise load from beside the operator's global config.

variables.name: PATH
variables.why: Never named in the shell: every `command -v` reads it, and that is how CrossRev decides a tool or a harness is installed. The port resolves it explicitly, so the name is in the table.

variables.name: RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT
variables.why: The only signal separating a GitHub-hosted runner from a self-hosted one and from a laptop, and so the one that decides whether a missing secret is a refusal.

variables.name: TMPDIR
variables.why: Where auth_login writes the App registration page and the redirect file it waits on. Read as ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} with the trailing slash trimmed, and assigned nowhere in the shell, so the value is the operator's.

variables.name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
variables.why: Where the operator config, the App keys and the token ledger live.

variables.name: XDG_DATA_HOME
variables.why: Opencode's staging lever, and not CrossRev's variable at all: exporting it reaches everything XDG-aware the same process runs afterwards, which is why the discard restores rather than unsets.

variables.name: XDG_STATE_HOME
variables.why: Where run logs, kept transcripts and resolve worktrees live.
